title: Synthetic: checkout latency after a release
text: SYNTHETIC SAMPLE FOR SMOKE TESTS ONLY. At 14:02 UTC we rolled out a new release of the checkout service. Within minutes p99 latency tripled and error rates climbed. Dashboards showed the connection pool to the primary database was fully used because the release removed a cache layer, so every request now hit the database. On-call engineers detected the problem through a latency alert and rolled back the release at 14:31. Afterward the team added a canary stage that compares database query volume before promoting a release to all servers.

title: Synthetic: expired TLS certificate drops API traffic
text: SYNTHETIC SAMPLE FOR SMOKE TESTS ONLY. Partner API traffic fell to near zero at 03:10 UTC. Clients reported handshake failures. The cause was an expired TLS certificate on the edge load balancer; the renewal job had been silently failing for weeks because a credential it used had been rotated. An engineer was paged by an external uptime probe and installed a new certificate manually in 40 minutes. The team now alerts when any certificate is within 21 days of expiry and tests the renewal job in staging.

title: Synthetic: replica lag causes stale reads
text: SYNTHETIC SAMPLE FOR SMOKE TESTS ONLY. Users saw old profile data after saving changes. Database replication lag grew to eleven minutes after a bulk backfill job saturated the primary's write capacity. Reads were routed to replicas that were falling behind. The incident was found when support tickets spiked. Engineers paused the backfill and temporarily routed reads to the primary. The fix was rate limiting the backfill and adding a lag-aware router that avoids replicas more than five seconds behind.

title: Synthetic: DNS misconfiguration makes service unreachable
text: SYNTHETIC SAMPLE FOR SMOKE TESTS ONLY. After a routine DNS change, the main domain stopped resolving for about a quarter of users. A record was edited manually and a trailing dot was missing, which pointed the name at an invalid target. Monitoring detected failed resolution from several regions. The engineer reverted the record, but cached answers kept the outage alive until TTLs expired. The team moved DNS changes into reviewed code with validation and lowered TTLs before planned changes.

title: Synthetic: queue backlog after traffic spike
text: SYNTHETIC SAMPLE FOR SMOKE TESTS ONLY. A marketing email drove a traffic spike ten times above normal. Workers consuming the order queue could not keep up, the backlog grew to two million messages, and customers waited hours for confirmation emails. Autoscaling was capped by a conservative maximum instance setting. Engineers raised the limit, added workers, and drained the queue in three hours. Prevention included load testing before campaigns and alerts on queue age rather than queue depth.

title: Synthetic: memory leak crashes search nodes
text: SYNTHETIC SAMPLE FOR SMOKE TESTS ONLY. Search nodes began restarting every few hours with out-of-memory errors. A regression in a new library version leaked memory when handling long queries. Restarts caused cascading load on the remaining nodes. An alert on restart count paged the team, who pinned the previous library version and redeployed. A heap profile later identified the leak. The team added memory growth alerts and a soak test to their release checklist.
